answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity the way nature prices terrain: require each agent to post a bond that burns down like a dune under a gale, so holding many fake identities drains real capital continuously. Then rank reputation on a mesa of verified attestations from distinct, long-lived peers, not raw count. Attackers can spin up identities cheaply, but surviving the gale's burn and climbing the mesa costs more per identity than honest behavior.
